title: Tamsin and the Cipher
premise: Felix Zhou, a small-town coroner with a private gift for spotting murder disguised as accident, receives a retainer from a dying woman named Tamsin Voss to prove that her own death — scheduled for the following week — will be a genuine accident, not murder. Digging into her family's past, Felix uncovers an inheritance cipher hidden in thirty-year-old coroner's records: proof that her father's 'accidental' death was staged by the family trust's executor, who now needs Tamsin dead to bury the secret forever. As Felix races to decode the cipher before the arranged 'accident,' he must choose between exposing the truth and protecting Tamsin, whom he has come to love. In the end, Felix fakes her death using his own forensic mastery, letting the executor confess to a murder that never happened — and the two of them walk away invisible together.
about_author: Ines Eriksen is the pen name of a former rural hospital administrator who spent a decade reading death certificates in three counties. She writes quiet mysteries about people whose jobs put them close to the dead, and lives somewhere north of the fog line with an uncooperative cat.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A frail stranger, Tamsin Voss, visits Felix's basement office and pays triple to hire him for a crime that hasn't occurred yet: she believes someone will stage her death as an accident within ten days, and wants him to prove it afterward. Felix, who values invisibility above all, almost refuses — until he recognizes the handwriting on her father's old death certificate. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Paper
chapters.summary: POV Felix, with interludes from Tamsin's journal. Pulling archived records, Felix finds three deaths from 1994 sharing one witness: Aldous Crane, executor of the Voss trust. Tamsin reveals the family cipher her father taught her, hidden in the margins of his ledgers, which she can no longer read alone. Their late nights decoding forge an intimacy neither expected. Emotional beat: love kindling against professional duty.

chapters.title: The Arranged Hour
chapters.summary: POV alternating Felix and Tamsin. The cipher cracks: it names Crane and details how he staged the father's fall — and predicts Tamsin's own, at the cliff road, on Thursday. When Felix confronts Crane, the executor calmly reveals he knows Felix's history of unofficial investigations and offers him hush money, then threatens to expose him. That night Tamsin disappears, leaving only the cipher book. Emotional beat: terror and betrayal at the climax's edge.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix finds Tamsin alive — she fled to force Crane's hand early — and proposes a desperate gambit: they stage her drowning so convincingly that Crane, believing the deed done, comes to collect and confesses to Felix's hidden recorder. The trap works; police arrive to arrest a man who murdered no one that night but confessed to murders thirty years old. Tamsin, legally dead, chooses exile with Felix. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into freedom, and love chosen over duty.
